title: Verifier‑Grounded Evaluation of LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: A Preregistered NetConfig‑Semantic Study (estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline)
abstract: We report a fully preregistered, artifact‑anchored paired experiment (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1; preregistration SHA‑256 7db1663cf3982c8ea1e16c3dd7c0348f356bb4cbe3978ecc75bb59fdedb71a37) whose preregistered estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (i.e., verifier consistency under identical canonical inputs, not independent generative reliability). Using a deterministic validator and template‑driven intent→config tasks (N = 120), we generated one canonical LLM candidate per task (shared_initial_candidate per pair) and reused it for both the deterministic template baseline and the LLM guarded condition. Results (archived): baseline = 120/120 verifier passes; guarded (gpt-5-mini, shared seed) = 120/120; paired difference = 0.00; 95% bootstrap CI [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729); exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. We publish exhaustive execution and scoring artifacts (per‑file SHA‑256s) and use them to (i) explain—by direct reference to archived response and validator traces—why the confirmatory paired contrast is degenerate, and (ii) propose runnable, artifact‑grounded modifications (independent_per_condition sampling, multi‑seed confirmatory designs, validator diversification) that answer the operational question practitioners typically require (independent LLM reliability) while preserving reproducibility.

sections.introduction: Correctly translating high‑level operator intent into low‑level device configuration is a core NetOps function where semantic correctness (reachability, ACL preservation, safe transient states) is safety‑critical. We preregistered a paired confirmatory test whose explicit estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (verifier response difference when identical canonical candidates are scored under two conditions). This paper (1) publishes the complete artifact bundle required for byte‑for‑byte reproduction (execution/execution_manifest.json and per‑file SHA‑256s), (2) reports the preregistered confirmatory outcome using archived scoring traces, and (3) uses the archived evidence to diagnose why the confirmatory contingency is degenerate and to recommend deterministic, runnable reruns that estimate independent generative reliability. Key contribution: an artifact‑grounded methodology and diagnosis that clarify what a verifier‑grounded confirmatory test measures—and what it does not—so operators and researchers choose sampling semantics matched to their operational question.
sections.related_work: Verifier‑grounded evaluation. Offline configuration analyzers (Batfish and successors) provide deterministic reachability and ACL analysis from static configs and are widely used for pre‑deployment validation (e.g., Batfish evolution; doi:10.1145/3603269.3604866). LLM→NetOps literature commonly couples generation to deterministic verifiers in a generate–validate–repair loop; experimental conclusions strongly depend on (A) sampling semantics (single canonical vs independent draws), (B) repair budgets, and (C) validator scope. Prior empirical work shows most repair gains occur in the first few iterations and that orchestration often matters more than model identity for repair outcomes. Published surveys and intent→config studies motivate verifier grounding but also highlight that independent sampling is required to estimate deployed stochastic reliability (see cited corpus).
sections.methodology: Preregistration and frozen design. The study preregistration (CAND‑2026‑001‑NetConfig‑Semantic‑v1; SHA‑256 7db1663cf398...) specified: N = 120 paired tasks (40 per topology class), primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, confirmatory generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one canonical LLM generation per task reused across both conditions), deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version 5.0), and the exact analysis plan (paired_binary_analysis_v1; bootstrap 10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Task synthesis. Tasks were programmatically generated from a deterministic template bank (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5). Each task manifest encodes: initial_state, expected_final_state, explicit required_sequence, per‑task workflow_policies (e.g., must_be_down_for_fields, minimum_active_in_groups), allowed_touched_fields, and a difficulty annotation. Validator and scoring. The validator enforces transient safety constraints and final_state assertions; scoring used rule full_intent_constraint_validation (binary pass only if all required commands and transient constraints are satisfied). Execution accounting (artifact evidence). The run used declared_model_version = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 a40e96e212ab87da...). Per the archived manifest: planned_episode_count = 240; completed_episode_count = 240; model_calls_used = 120; maximum_model_calls = 240. Model_calls_used = 120 because a single canonical generation was produced per task and reused for both scoring episodes (see execution/responses/*-shared-initial.txt, execution/provider_calls/* and execution/execution_manifest.json for per‑file SHA‑256s). Example canonical candidate artifact: execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 8f38c8becd7e1e36...). Representative validator trace: execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA‑256 0d56c1add7c5a57f...). Contamination checks. Preregistered exact‑match and normalized n‑gram heuristics were run and recorded (analysis/contamination_summary.csv); absence of a heuristic flag is not conclusive proof of zero pretraining exposure.
sections.results: Confirmatory counts and archived statistics (exact): baseline_success_count = 120/120; guarded_success_count (gpt‑5‑mini shared_initial) = 120/120. Paired 2×2 contingency (archived analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 9f25790c...): n_11 = 120; n_10 = 0; n_01 = 0; n_00 = 0. Primary estimator (mean guarded_i − baseline_i) = 0.00. Bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) = [0.00, 0.00]. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. All per‑episode scoring JSONs and model provider traces are published and SHA‑256‑fingerprinted in the execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json). Representative artifacts supporting the reported numbers: analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 9c77c96f...), analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 9f25790c...), paired_difference_figure.svg (SHA‑256 ae5b8e0c...). Model_call accounting: the shared_initial design causes model_calls_used = 120 because each task produced one canonical candidate that was scored in both conditions; the manifested provider call traces for shared_initial generation are archived under execution/provider_calls/*.json (see manifest).
sections.discussion:
Why the confirmatory contingency is degenerate (artifact‑visible causal chain). The run implemented preregistered generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate: a single canonical LLM candidate per task was deterministically archived and reused for both baseline and guarded scoring episodes (execution/responses/*-shared-initial.txt). Because the validator is deterministic and tasks encode explicit required_sequences matched by template‑aligned candidates, identical inputs necessarily yield identical pass/fail outputs; the artifact traces (execution/scoring/*.json) show parsed_command_count, required_command_count, normalized_configuration and validation_after.valid = true for these canonical candidates. Thus the confirmatory result correctly answers the preregistered estimand (validator consistency under identical inputs) but does not estimate independent generative reliability.

Operational question vs preregistered estimand (artifact‑grounded mapping). Table mapping (paper Table 1, artifacts: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/condition_summary.csv):
- Operational question practitioners want: "What is the probability that independently sampled LLM outputs will satisfy verifier constraints (deployment reliability)?" — requires independent_per_condition sampling or multi‑seed designs (not executed here). 
- Preregistered estimand tested here: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (verifier response difference when identical canonical candidates are scored under two conditions) — answered by shared_initial_candidate design and archived traces. 
- Why shared_initial_candidate answers the latter but not the former: determinism of validator + identical canonical inputs ⇒ identical scores; archive demonstrates identical canonical files were used across both conditions (execution/responses/*-shared-initial.txt, execution/scoring/* JSON traces).

Runnable artifact‑grounded next steps (explicit, not executed here). The published bundle permits immediate deterministic reruns that answer independent reliability: (1) independent_per_condition rerun — generate separate LLM seeds per condition per task using the archived task_manifest (execution/task_manifest.jsonl) and execution/model_configuration.json; (2) multi‑seed confirmatory design — generate K≥3 independent seeds per condition and estimate per‑condition pass probabilities with bootstrap CIs; (3) validator diversification — add a second verifier and report intersection/union pass rates. All required artifacts to perform these reruns deterministically are archived (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 a40e96e2..., execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 ee556252..., execution/provider_calls/*.json and execution/scoring/*.json). We emphasize these are proposed reruns—artifact‑grounded next steps—not new experiments invented for this manuscript.
sections.conclusion: We provide a fully preregistered, artifact‑anchored verifier‑grounded paired experiment and publish the exhaustive execution and scoring traces (with per‑file SHA‑256s) required for byte‑for‑byte reproduction. The preregistered estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline) was intentionally operationalized via shared_initial_candidate semantics; the archived evidence shows identical canonical candidates were scored under both conditions, producing n_11 = 120 and a paired difference of 0.00. That outcome is correct for the preregistered estimand but does not speak to independent LLM generative reliability in deployment. We provide artifact‑grounded, runnable modifications (independent_per_condition, multi‑seed sampling, validator diversification) that convert the current reproducible pipeline into one that answers the operational question practitioners typically need, and we release all artifacts and hashes needed to run or audit those reruns deterministically.

No human manually edited technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. Confirmatory generation semantics and model_call accounting: preregistered generation_semantics = 'shared_initial_candidate' (one canonical LLM candidate per task reused for both baseline and guarded scoring) which caused model_calls_used = 120 (see execution/execution_manifest.json and execution/responses/*-shared-initial.txt artifacts). limitations: Controlled synthetic tasks: template‑driven tasks encode explicit required_sequences and workflow_policies that favour canonical solutions and reduce open‑language generalizability.

Confirmatory shared_initial semantics: the preregistered shared_initial_candidate design intentionally removed generation variance and therefore precluded estimation of independent generative reliability.

Single canonical seed for confirmatory test: primary analysis used one canonical seed per task; preregistered exploratory multi‑seed analyses were not included in the confirmatory inference reported here.
Validator–task coupling: deterministic validator enforces task template constraints; template alignment can elevate pass rates relative to open distributions.

Possible training‑data exposure: preregistered contamination heuristics found no flags under thresholds applied, but absence of a flag is not proof of zero exposure to related artifacts in pretraining.
Single‑model, single‑validator run: results apply to gpt‑5‑mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 as archived and do not generalize without reruns under different models/validators.
